paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers visited the town library with Teacher Kim. A woman in a blue jacket met them at the door. "Good morning," she said. "I am the manager of this library." "My job is to look after the books and the people who work here."

"What do you do all day?" asked Lily. "I choose new books," said the manager. "I read the newspaper to find news about our town." "I also talk to schools, like yours." "Is a library a business?" asked Leo. "No, we do not sell books," she said. "The town pays for the library, and everyone can use it."

Then a man with a long red scarf stood up in the story room. "This is our guest," said the manager. "He is an actor, and he reads a story to the children today." The actor read about a queen and a small bird. The queen in the story wore a gold crown. He used a high voice for the queen and a low voice for the bird. Mia laughed, and May listened with her chin on her hand. "Is acting your job?" asked Mia after the story. "Yes, I work in plays at night," said the actor. "In the day, I read stories to children."

Teacher Kim had a game for the Explorers. "Guess the thing from my words," she said. "It has big pages and small letters." "People read it every morning to find the news." "A newspaper!" said May. "Now guess the person," said Teacher Kim. "She is in today's story, and she has a gold crown." "The queen!" said Leo. "Right!" said Teacher Kim.

Before they left, the manager gave each child a card. "If you come again, please say hello," she said. Lily wrote about the two jobs for Explorers' Blog that evening. Leo drew a queen with a crown, and he drew an actor with a red scarf. "Maybe I want to be an actor," he said.
